data.title: Preferred Bank sees Q4 noninterest expense at $23M-$24M as deposit market stays 'very, very competitive'
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Preferred Bank (PFBC) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Preferred Bank's third quarter net income was $32.9 million or $2.73 per share." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • "This quarter was negatively affected by a $2.1 million recovery of interest income." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • "Deposits grew $77 million or 1.2% on a linked quarter basis" and "the deposit market is very, very competitive" with management expecting this "will likely go into the year 2027." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • "Loans for the quarter decreased $40 million after we placed a large credit on the for sale status" and "this time, our pipeline seems to be very solid, and we're very hopeful that in the fourth quarter to have a good solid growth." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • "This quarter, net interest margin reported 3.49%. Without this $2.1 million adjustment, it would have been 3.60%." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • "Resolution of nonaccrual loans is continuing but slower than what we hope for" and "several credit was scheduled to be resolved in this quarter are stuck in the court proceedings" with timing pushed to "fourth quarter next year." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • "We are pleased with our consistent cost control of overhead even under a very inflationary period." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)

Outlook

  • "Going forward, we see a stable interest rate market condition. If the Fed fund is going to adjust higher then it will further benefit our net interest margin as we, Preferred Bank, is an asset-sensitive bank." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • "Unlike at the beginning of the third quarter when we reported in our last conference phone call, but this time, our pipeline seems to be very solid" with the team "very hopeful" for "good solid growth" in Q4. (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • "On a go-forward basis, I would say for Q4, look for somewhere between $23 million and $24 million" of noninterest expense. (Executive VP & CFO Edward Czajka)

Financial Results

  • "Preferred Bank's third quarter net income was $32.9 million or $2.73 per share." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • "Deposits grew $77 million or 1.2% on a linked quarter basis" while "Loans for the quarter decreased $40 million" following moving "a large credit" to "for sale status." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • "Net interest margin reported 3.49%" and management quantified that "Without this $2.1 million adjustment, it would have been 3.60%." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • "We had a decrease in professional services, primarily legal fees" and "our incentive compensation accrual was lower this quarter than it was in the prior quarter due to profitability being slightly less." (Executive VP & CFO Czajka)

Q&A

  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler & Co., Research Division: "how much in the way of CDs you have maturing here in the fourth quarter and the weighted average roll-off and roll-on rates"? Executive VP & CFO Czajka: "We have just under $1.7 million maturing in the fourth quarter... Weighted average yield is 3.81%. Those are likely to come on anywhere between 3.75% to 4% as they roll over."
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler & Co., Research Division: asked for September deposit cost and spot margin, plus deposit beta expectations if rates rise; Executive VP & CFO Czajka: "Total deposit cost was 3.06% for the month of September and the spot margin was 3.58%" and deposit costs should reprice "Definitely slower" because "Our focus is on keeping the costs under control."
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler & Co., Research Division: asked criticized/classified levels, NPA disposal timing, and loss concerns; Executive VP & Chief Risk Officer Nick Pi: "the total classified loan was $177.6 million, which covers classifieds plus $11.5 million OREO" and while bankruptcy timelines depend on court actions, "we do believe all these BK proceedings is heading in the right direction" and "hopefully, by Q4, there will be a couple of large loans will be disposed."
  • Andrew Liesch, StoneX Financial, Inc., Research Division: asked what drove weaker loan growth and whether higher rates are delaying projects; President & COO Wellington Chen: loan growth reflected "some unexpected payoffs" and production "wasn't as robust as the second quarter production," while "with the higher rate, people are a little bit more conscientious about the project itself."
  • Andrew Liesch, StoneX Financial, Inc., Research Division: asked if lower expenses were unique and where Q4 should start; Executive VP & CFO Czajka: "decrease in professional services, primarily legal fees" plus lower incentive comp, and "for Q4, look for somewhere between $23 million and $24 million."
  • Andrew Terrell, Stephens Inc., Research Division: asked if end-of-period deposit growth was transitory and about deposit growth/costs; Executive VP & CFO Czajka: "it's a good launch point for the next quarter" and the quarter-end/average gap reflected broker deposits "maturing and coming on late in the quarter." Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Yu: deposit pricing is "all over the place" and said customers shift from CDs to Treasuries because "a 5% Treasury became 5.65% effective yield" in California after-tax terms.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were neutral to slightly negative, pressing on funding costs, betas, and criticized loans, with questions concentrated on deposits, loan growth softness, and timing of problem-loan resolutions.
  • Management tone was slightly positive but cautious on deposits and credit timing, emphasizing discipline and constraints, including "the deposit market is very, very competitive" and loan resolutions "stuck in the court proceedings." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Yu)
  • Versus the prior quarter, management language shifted from optimism on asset-resolution progress to more emphasis on delays and a more competitive deposit backdrop, moving from "Non-performing loans during the quarter has been reduced $70 million or 41.5%" (Q2) to "Resolution of nonaccrual loans is continuing but slower than what we hope for" (Q3). (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Yu)

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Q2 highlighted rapid criticized/NPL improvement and stronger loan growth, including "Loan increased $125 million or 2.0%" and "Non-performing loans during the quarter has been reduced $70 million or 41.5%." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu, Q2)
  • Q3 emphasized softer balances and a reversal-related margin impact, with "Loans for the quarter decreased $40 million" and "net interest margin reported 3.49%. Without this $2.1 million adjustment, it would have been 3.60%." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Yu, Q3)
  • On credit cleanup timing, Q2 flagged bankruptcy uncertainty—"the exact timing of the resolution will be at the mercy of our legal system"—while Q3 reported that some resolutions "are stuck in the court proceedings" and pushed out to "fourth quarter next year." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Yu)
  • Analyst focus remained deposit-cost centric across both calls, but Q3 questions leaned more into spot costs/rollovers and court-driven resolution timing.

Risks and Concerns

  • "The deposit market is very, very competitive" and management said customers are allocating cash to alternatives, including that "many of our customers deposit -- invest extra funds into the treasuries." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Li Yu)
  • Credit-resolution timing risk remained tied to legal processes, with multiple references to bankruptcy court timelines and that resolutions are "stuck in the court proceedings." (Chairman, CEO & Corporate Secretary Yu)
  • Loan-growth execution risk was tied to payoffs and delayed fundings, with growth impacted by "some unexpected payoffs" and pipeline fundings that "carry over to this quarter." (President & COO Wellington Chen)

Final Takeaway

Preferred Bank framed Q3 around a reversal-related drag on reported net interest margin, modest linked-quarter deposit growth amid what management called a “very, very competitive” market, and slower-than-hoped nonaccrual resolution due to bankruptcy court timing. Management pointed to a “very solid” pipeline and expressed hope for improved Q4 loan growth, while the CFO guided Q4 noninterest expense to $23 million–$24 million and reiterated deposit-cost discipline as a key operating priority.

data.title: 3 E Network Technology sets 2-for-1 share consolidation for Oct. 30
data.description:
• 3 E Network Technology (MASK) announced Friday that its board approved a 2-for-1 share consolidation, effective October 30, 2026.
  • Each two Class A or Class B ordinary shares will be combined into one share, with fractional shares rounded up to the next whole share.
  • The stock will continue trading on a split-adjusted basis on Nasdaq under the same ticker, MASK.
  • The outstanding Class A shares will fall to ~2.62M from 5.23M, while Class B shares will decline to 11.6K from 23.2K.
  • The company will also halve the number of authorized Class A shares from 100M to 50M and Class B shares from 50M to 25M, while doubling the par value to $0.005 per share.
  • The stock traded ~2.29% lower to ~$0.81 in the after-hours session.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: 3 things to look out for on Monday
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages finished in the red on Friday as technology stocks continued to lag amid artificial intelligence spending fears and a continued rise in oil prices due to geopolitical issues.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) lost -1.2%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) finished -0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) slipped -0.2%.

Here are three things to look out for on Monday:

  • Monday brings more earnings reports, with Wall Street focused on Verizon Communications (VZ) ahead of the opening bell. Shares of the telecom giant are expected to deliver their latest quarterly results, giving investors an early read on the company’s performance and the broader sector.
  • In other earnings-related news, market participants will be watching Nucor Corporation’s (NUE) latest results, which are expected after the closing bell on Monday. The steel producer’s report should offer insight into industrial demand and the broader materials sector.
  • On the economic calendar, traders will be watching the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index, due shortly after the opening bell on Monday. The regional survey offers an early snapshot of manufacturing conditions in Texas and is often viewed as a timely indicator for broader U.S. industrial activity.

data.title: U.S. stocks end in weekly losses as a tech stock selloff drags markets
data.description:
U.S. major stock indexes finished mostly lower on Friday due to a continued technology selloff that rattled the markets and the rise in oil prices from the ongoing U.S.-Iran war.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) closed -0.5%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) finished -0.2%, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) ended -1.2%.

Week-to-date, the S&P 500 was -0.5%, the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.7%, and the Dow (DJI) gained 0.4%.

Big tech stocks, including Tesla (TSLA) -0.6%, Amazon (AMZN) -0.9%, Alphabet (GOOGL) -1.1%, and Meta (META) -0.9%, continued to suffer.

“This week was a good one for the Dow, the Russell 2000, defense stocks, oil, U.S. government bonds, and their ETFs; heck, it was even a good week for biotech,” said Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research.

“The crypto boogeyman was flat. Despite which there is a caterwaul of crying in the casino, which can only be because people are far too concentrated in the same high-beta semiconductor and component stocks. I think semiconductors and everything else are headed up into year-end.  Possibly without those who were shaken out this week,” King added.

In geopolitics, U.S. President Donald Trump accused Iran of “doing everything they can to drive up the price of oil” prior to the midterm election.

Oil prices rose after reports that the U.S. and Israel could be drawing plans for attacks on Iran.

Crude oil futures (CL1:COM) rose to $103.57, while Brent (CO1:COM) was also higher at $117.02 per barrel.

On the economic side, the October U.S. PMI Composite fell to 57.6, as expected, according to S&P Global on Friday. In addition, the U.S. Manufacturing PMI rose higher than consensus, while the U.S. Services PMI was slightly lower than expected.

Over to the bond market, yields were slightly higher. The 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) rose 4 basis points to 5.00%, while the 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) was 4 basis points higher at 4.69%. The 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) rose 5 basis points to 5.33%.

data.title: S&P 500 ends lower for week as AI spending concerns and rising oil prices weigh
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages finished in the red on Friday as technology stocks continued to lag amid artificial intelligence spending fears and a continued rise in oil prices due to geopolitical issues.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) slipped 1.2%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) declined 0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) edged down 0.2%.

The S&P 500 also declined 0.42% for the week.

Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman highlighted that this week was another period of rotation, with market breadth widening. That's a good thing for bull markets, generally. But this market is still tepid because the macro picture for oil and fuel more broadly is still in flux.

“The S&P is trading at its 10-year average forward PE despite record earnings growth. There's a lot of “pricing in” going on that I expect to unravel (in the bullish sense) if we get great earnings out of big tech next week, namely Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet (GOOGL),” Bowman added.

From a sector-level perspective, eight S&P 500 sectors ended the week in positive territory, while three finished in the red.

Energy (XLE) and Healthcare (XLV) were the strongest-performing sectors this week, with gains of 1.57% and 1.5%, respectively.

Bowman also noted that healthcare was one of the top gainers this week because earnings season favored the sector, which is good to see because that means breadth is improving.

The analyst added that the energy sector also had a solid week, partially because of the continued rotation, but also because it's tied to oil prices, which climbed this week. News of escalating tensions in the Middle East and attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure have pushed global energy markets higher, and he expects XLE to continue higher as long as the war persists.

Conversely, Communication Services (XLC) and Industrials (XLI) posted the weakest weekly performances, falling 4.31% and 1.86%, respectively.

Bowman concluded that the communication services sector was down on news from Meta (META), which accounts for such a significant portion of the fund that its 9% weekly decline dragged down the entire sector. Earnings were not so bad, although XLC is the only one of the 11 sectors with a negative forward EPS growth projection. With 10-year Treasury yields still sitting at around 5%, it just doesn't cut it, and it makes sense for investors to rotate out when cyclical stocks come under pressure.

“The same applies to industrials, which also have heavy exposures to cyclicals, and the losses this week came largely from data center-adjacent companies.”

data.title: U.S. drilling rig count flat for second straight week in Baker Hughes survey
data.description:
The number of oil and gas rigs actively drilling in the U.S. remained unchanged at 603, Baker Hughes reported Friday in its latest weekly survey.

The number of active drilling rigs targeting crude oil in the U.S. added 1 to 460 in the week ended October 23, while gas rigs dropped 1 to 132 and rigs categorized as miscellaneous stayed flat at 11.

The total rig count was up by 53, or 9.6%, compared to the same time last year, while the number of rigs drilling for oil rose by 40, or 9.5%, from a year ago, and gas rigs gained 11, or 9.1%, from a year earlier.

Rigs targeting oil in the Permian Basin remained unchanged in the past week at 272, while the Eagle Ford gained 2 to 43 and the Williston Basin added 1 to 31.

data.title: Instacart gains on report it's in talks to sell itself
data.description:
Instacart (CART) jumped 10% on a report that the grocery store delivery company is in discussions to try to sell itself.

Instarcart (CART) has been working with an investment bank to consider its options and has had preliminary discussions with DoorDash (DASH) and Uber (UBER),  according to a report from The Information on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Shares of Uber fell 3.7%, while DoorDash dropped 3.8%.
